name: Urinary system
description: Kidneys, adrenal glands, renal vessels, ureters, urinary bladder and urethra.

groups.label: Urinary system
groups.tip: Follow the urine: kidney, ureter, bladder, urethra. The kidneys, adrenal glands and ureters sit behind the belly lining, against your back wall.

groups.label: Kidneys and adrenal glands
groups.tip: A WET BED lists the kidney jobs: Acid balance, Water, Electrolytes, Toxins, Blood pressure, Erythropoietin and vitamin D. The adrenal cortex makes salt, sugar and sex hormones.

groups.label: Renal vessels
groups.tip: At the kidney notch, think VAP from front to back: vein, artery, pelvis. The long left kidney vein crosses in front of the aorta.

groups.label: Ureters, bladder and urethra
groups.tip: Water under the bridge: the ureter passes under the uterine artery in females and under the sperm duct in males.

content.origin: Kidney is an old English word of unknown origin. The Latin ren and the Greek nephros also mean kidney, which is why we say renal and nephron.
content.location: High on the back wall of your belly, behind the gut lining, roughly from T12 to L3. The right one sits a little lower because the liver is above it.
content.description: Shaped like a bean, about 10 to 12 centimetres long, with a notch on the inner side where vessels and the urine funnel pass through.
content.function: It filters your blood through about a million tiny filters, the nephrons, to make urine. It also helps control blood pressure, red blood cell making and vitamin D.
content.mnemonic: A WET BED lists its jobs: Acid balance, Water, Electrolytes, Toxins, Blood pressure, Erythropoietin and vitamin D.
content.clinical: A kidney stone that slips into the ureter causes waves of severe pain. The pain often runs from the lower back round to the groin.
content.hint: The bean-shaped organ on the right side of the back wall of the belly, with a small gland on top and vessels in its inner notch.

questions.text: Why does the right kidney usually sit lower than the left?
options: The aorta is on the right
questions.explanation: The big liver takes up the space on the right, so the right kidney sits a little lower.

questions.text: Which kidney hormone tells the body to make more red blood cells?
questions.explanation: When the blood carries too little oxygen, the kidneys release erythropoietin. It tells the bone marrow to make more red cells.

questions.text: What is the tiny filtering unit of the kidney called?
questions.explanation: Each kidney has about a million nephrons. Each one filters blood and makes a little urine.

content.origin: From the Latin ad, meaning near, and ren, meaning kidney. Its other name, suprarenal, means above the kidney.
content.location: Sitting on the top of the right kidney, tucked behind the big vein, the inferior vena cava, and the liver.
content.description: A small, pyramid-shaped gland, like a little hat on the kidney. It has an outer layer, the cortex, and an inner core, the medulla.
content.function: The cortex makes hormones for salt and water balance, for handling stress and sugar, and some sex hormones. The medulla makes adrenaline for fight or flight.
content.mnemonic: The cortex makes salt, sugar and sex hormones. The medulla is in the middle and makes adrenaline.
content.clinical: In Addison's disease, the cortex stops making enough hormones. In Cushing's syndrome, it makes too much cortisol.
content.hint: The small hormone-making cap sitting on top of the right bean-shaped organ.

questions.text: Which hormones does the adrenal medulla make?
questions.explanation: The medulla pumps out adrenaline and noradrenaline, getting you ready for fight or flight.

questions.text: Addison's disease is failure of which part?
questions.explanation: In Addison's disease the adrenal cortex fails, so there is too little cortisol and aldosterone.

content.origin: From the Latin ren, meaning kidney. Renal means of the kidney.
content.location: It leaves the right side of the aorta at about L1 to L2 and runs behind the big vein, the inferior vena cava, to reach the right kidney.
content.description: Longer than the left renal artery, because the aorta lies to the left of the middle. Near the kidney it splits into smaller branches.
content.function: It brings fresh, oxygen-rich blood into the kidney to be filtered. The two kidneys take about a fifth to a quarter of all the blood the heart pumps at rest.
content.mnemonic: At the kidney notch, from front to back, think VAP: Vein, Artery, Pelvis.
content.clinical: If this artery narrows, the kidney thinks blood pressure is low and releases more renin. This drives blood pressure up.
content.hint: The vessel leaving the side of the main belly artery near L1 and running behind the big vein to the right kidney.

questions.text: The renal arteries branch from which vessel?
questions.explanation: Both renal arteries come off the sides of the abdominal aorta, at about L1 to L2.

questions.text: A narrowed renal artery usually causes what?
questions.explanation: Less blood reaches the kidney, so it releases more renin, and that pushes blood pressure up.

content.origin: From the Latin ren, kidney, and vena, vein. It is the vein of the kidney.
content.location: A short hop from the notch of the right kidney, in front of the renal artery, straight into the big vein, the inferior vena cava.
content.description: Very short, only about two to three centimetres, because the big vein sits just to the right of the middle.
content.function: It carries cleaned blood out of the kidney and into the inferior vena cava, on its way back to the heart.
content.mnemonic: Left renal vein is long and crosses the aorta. The right renal vein is a short stub, since the big vein is right next door.
content.clinical: Because this vein is so short, surgeons usually take the left kidney from a living donor. Its longer vein is easier to join.
content.hint: The short vessel carrying blood straight from the right kidney into the large vein beside it.

content.origin: From the Greek ourein, meaning to pass urine.
content.location: It runs from the right kidney down the back wall of the belly, over the psoas muscle, across the rim of the pelvis and into the back of the bladder.
content.description: A narrow muscular tube about 25 to 30 centimetres long. It enters the bladder on a slant, which works like a valve to stop urine flowing back up.
content.function: It carries urine from the kidney down to the bladder. Its muscle squeezes in waves, called peristalsis, like squeezing toothpaste along a tube.
content.mnemonic: Water under the bridge. The ureter passes under the uterine artery in females and under the sperm duct in males.
content.clinical: Kidney stones get stuck at its three narrow points: where it leaves the kidney, at the pelvic rim, and where it enters the bladder. This causes intense pain.
content.hint: The long thin tube running down from the right kidney to the back of the bladder.

questions.text: Where do kidney stones most often get stuck in the ureter?
questions.explanation: The ureter narrows where it leaves the kidney, at the rim of the pelvis and where it enters the bladder.

questions.text: How is urine moved along the ureter?
options: By waves of smooth muscle squeezing
By muscles you control at will
questions.explanation: Smooth muscle in the ureter wall squeezes in waves, called peristalsis, pushing urine down even when you lie flat.

content.origin: Kidney is an old English word whose roots nobody is sure of. The Latin ren gives us renal, and the Greek nephros gives us nephron.
content.location: High on the back wall of your belly, behind the gut lining, a little higher than the right kidney. The stomach, spleen, pancreas and colon lie in front of it.
content.description: A bean-shaped organ, about 10 to 12 centimetres long. Inside, an outer layer and inner cones drain urine into a funnel that leads to the ureter.
content.function: It cleans your blood and makes urine, balancing your water, salts and acid. It also releases hormones for blood pressure and red blood cells.
content.mnemonic: Remember its jobs with A WET BED: Acid, Water, Electrolytes, Toxins, Blood pressure, Erythropoietin, vitamin D.
content.clinical: Kidney stones can form here and pass down the ureter. As they move, they cause sharp, coming-and-going pain from the loin to the groin.
content.hint: The bean-shaped organ on the left side of the back wall of the belly, with a small gland on top and vessels in its inner notch.

content.origin: From the Latin ad, near, and ren, kidney. It is also called suprarenal, which means above the kidney.
content.location: On the upper inner edge of the left kidney, reaching down toward its notch. It sits behind the stomach and pancreas.
content.description: A small half-moon-shaped gland hugging the kidney. It has an outer cortex and an inner medulla, wrapped with the kidney in the same layer of tissue.
content.function: Its cortex makes aldosterone for salt and water, cortisol for stress and sugar, and some sex hormones. Its medulla makes adrenaline and noradrenaline.
content.mnemonic: Salt, sugar and sex come from the cortex. The medulla, in the middle, gives the adrenaline rush.
content.clinical: Two well-known cortex problems are Addison's disease, where too little hormone is made, and Cushing's syndrome, where there is too much cortisol.
content.hint: The small half-moon cap on the top inner edge of the left bean-shaped organ.

content.origin: From the Latin renalis, meaning of the kidney.
content.location: It leaves the left side of the aorta at about L1 to L2 and takes a short path to the notch of the left kidney.
content.description: Shorter than the right renal artery, because the aorta sits a little to the left. Near the kidney it splits into smaller branches.
content.function: It carries oxygen-rich blood to the left kidney for cleaning. Together the kidneys get about a fifth to a quarter of the heart's output at rest.
content.mnemonic: Vein, Artery, Pelvis, or VAP, is the order at the kidney notch from front to back.
content.clinical: A narrowed renal artery starves the kidney of blood, so it releases more renin. The result is high blood pressure that can be hard to control.
content.hint: The short vessel leaving the side of the main belly artery near L1 and entering the left kidney.

content.origin: From the Latin ren, kidney, and vena, vein.
content.location: It runs from the notch of the left kidney across the front of the aorta, just below the superior mesenteric artery, to reach the big vein on the right.
content.description: About three times longer than the right renal vein. The veins from the left testis or ovary and the left adrenal gland drain into it.
content.function: It carries cleaned blood from the left kidney back to the inferior vena cava, and on to the heart.
content.mnemonic: Left is long. The left renal vein crosses in front of the aorta to reach the big vein on the right.
content.clinical: It can be squeezed between the aorta and the artery above it, like a nut in a nutcracker. This can cause blood in the urine and swollen veins by the left testis.
content.hint: The long vessel from the left kidney that crosses in front of the main artery to reach the large vein on the right.

questions.text: Which renal vein is longer and crosses in front of the aorta?
options: Neither, both pass behind the aorta
questions.explanation: The left renal vein has to cross in front of the aorta to reach the big vein on the right, so it is longer.

questions.text: The vein from the left testis or ovary drains into which vessel?
questions.explanation: On the left, the gonadal vein empties into the left renal vein. On the right, it goes straight into the big vein.

content.origin: From the Greek oureter, based on ourein, to pass urine.
content.location: It runs from the left kidney down the back wall of the belly on the psoas muscle, crosses the rim of the pelvis and enters the back of the bladder.
content.description: A thin muscular tube about 25 to 30 centimetres long. It tunnels through the bladder wall on a slant, making a one-way valve.
content.function: It moves urine from the left kidney to the bladder in waves of muscle squeezing, so urine flows down even when you lie down.
content.mnemonic: Remember water under the bridge. The ureter runs under the uterine artery or the sperm duct.
content.clinical: A stone stuck at one of its three narrow points blocks the flow and causes renal colic, waves of severe pain from the loin to the groin.
content.hint: The long thin tube running down from the left kidney to the back of the bladder.

content.origin: From the Old English word for a bladder or blister. The Latin vesica and Greek kystis also mean bladder, as in cystitis.
content.location: Low in your pelvis, just behind the pubic bone. As it fills, it rises up into your lower belly.
content.description: A hollow, stretchy bag of muscle, like a balloon. On its floor is a smooth triangle, the trigone, between the two ureter openings and the urethra.
content.function: It stores urine, usually comfortably up to about 400 to 500 millilitres in adults. When you go, its wall muscle, the detrusor, squeezes it empty.
content.mnemonic: Trigone means triangle. Two ureters come in and one urethra goes out.
content.clinical: Cystitis, a bladder infection, is a very common urinary infection. If the bladder cannot empty, a thin tube called a catheter can drain it.
content.hint: The hollow muscular storage bag behind the pubic bone, filled by two tubes and emptied by one.

questions.text: What is the smooth triangle on the floor of the bladder called?
questions.explanation: The trigone is the triangle between the two ureter openings and the urethra opening.

questions.text: Which muscle squeezes to empty the bladder?
questions.explanation: The detrusor is the smooth muscle in the bladder wall. It squeezes to push urine out.

content.origin: From the Greek ourethra, from ourein, meaning to pass urine.
content.location: It runs from the neck of the bladder, through the prostate and the pelvic floor, then along the penis to the outside.
content.description: In males it is about 18 to 20 centimetres long, in four parts, and the longest part runs along the penis. In females it is only about four centimetres.
content.function: It carries urine from the bladder out of the body, and in males it carries semen too. A ring of muscle you control lets you hold on or let go.
content.mnemonic: The four male parts, from the bladder out, are P P M S: preprostatic, prostatic, membranous and spongy.
content.clinical: An enlarged prostate squeezes the part of the urethra inside it, giving a weak stream. The short female urethra is why women get more bladder infections.
content.hint: The outlet tube leading from the neck of the bladder through the prostate and along the penis.

questions.text: Which is the longest part of the male urethra?
questions.explanation: The spongy part runs the whole length of the penis, so it is the longest.

questions.text: An enlarged prostate mainly squeezes which part of the urethra?
questions.explanation: The prostatic part runs right through the prostate, so when the gland grows, it gets squeezed.

content.origin: From the Greek aorte, linked to a word meaning to lift. Ancient writers thought the heart hung from it.
content.location: It runs down the back wall of your belly, just left of the middle, in front of the spine and beside the big vein.
content.description: The body's main artery. In the belly it sends a branch to each kidney at about L1 to L2, then splits in two at about L4.
content.function: It carries oxygen-rich blood from the heart down to the belly, pelvis and legs, including both kidneys.
content.mnemonic: Artery on the left, vein on the right, lying side by side on the spine.
content.clinical: An aortic aneurysm is a dangerous ballooning of its wall. If it bursts, it causes massive bleeding.
content.hint: The main artery running down just left of the middle, sending a branch to each kidney.

content.origin: Vena cava is Latin for hollow vein. Inferior means lower, because it drains the lower body.
content.location: It runs up the back wall of your belly, to the right of the aorta, and passes through the diaphragm at T8.
content.description: The largest vein in the body. It starts at about L5, where the two big veins from the legs join.
content.function: It carries used blood from the lower body back to the right side of the heart. Both renal veins empty into it.
content.mnemonic: IVC is on the right side, like the right heart it returns to. The aorta keeps to the left.
content.clinical: Late in pregnancy, lying flat on the back lets the womb press on this vein. Blood pressure can drop and the mother may feel faint.
content.hint: The large vein to the right of the main artery, receiving both kidney veins.
